text.p: Miner and mining contractor Minproc Engineers Ltd said on Thursday the past year had been horrendous but the company was now focussed on growth.
"The past year was horrendous for Minproc," chairman Brettney Fogarty said in a statement.
"However, the loss represents the low water mark. Our balance sheet is rebuilt and we are now clearly focussed on growth and especially on increasing shareholder value."
Earlier the company reported a full year net loss of A$26.22 million, compared to a net profit of A$4.66 million in the previous corresponding period.

Fogarty said the company had achieved resolution of outstanding issues at the Yolanda nitrates project, the Indonesian Minahasa gold project and the lithium carbonate project at Greenbushes in Western Australia and had won shareholder approval for a major recapitalisation.

"Corporate restructuring and the solving of major operational problems is now complemented by the injection of new capital," Fogarty said of the plan which will see the injection of A$12.5 million in fresh capital.
The restructuring follows the company's announcement on September 9 that it had terminated its relationship with U.S. affiliate MinCorp Ltd and sold its 25 percent stake.

Minproc said termination of the MinCorp relationship allowed it to freely trade in the Americas and the Commonwealth of Independent States and also released it from past and future obligations to MinCorp.
Minproc shares closed four cents higher at 68 cents on turnover of 79,700 shares.
